In November 2021 ADS spun off LoyaltyOne as Loyalty Ventures Inc. (LTRN). On March 23, 2022 the remaining card-and-payments business rebranded as Bread Financial Holdings, Inc., with the common stock starting to trade on NYSE under the new ticker BFH on April 4, 2022. Today Bread Financial is a tech-forward financial services company headquartered in Columbus, Ohio (Wikipedia 2024 figures: $3.84B revenue, ~6,000 employees, $22.9B total assets, 135+ managed card programs across partners including Victoria's Secret, Wayfair, Williams-Sonoma, Academy Sports, HP, PlayStation, and the Crypto.com Visa Card). The developer surface lives under the Bread Pay BNPL brand at developer-facing properties docs.breadpayments.com (legacy "bread-classic" Merchant API) and platform-docs.breadpayments.com (next-generation "BreadPay Platform" APIs, OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials, hosted on https://api.platform.breadpayments.com/api), plus a JavaScript Bread SDK (preview + production CDN), iOS/Android mobile SDKs published as the Bread Financial Brand Partners SDKs on github.com/bppub, and platform integrations for Shopify, Magento 2, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Miva, Volusion, and Turbify. The corporate/holding side (private-label and co-brand cards issued through Comenity Bank and Comenity Capital Bank, plus high-yield savings, CDs, IRAs, and personal loans) is delivered through B2B partner integrations rather than a public developer portal.

The APIs support open banking integrations and financial technology applications.

Beacon PRO+ offers a REST API and Swagger-documented integration layer for contractor management software, ERP systems, and roofing business applications. Beacon was acquired by QXO in 2025.

name: Beazer Homes USA
description: Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (NYSE: BZH) is an Atlanta, Georgia-headquartered national homebuilder founded in 1985 and publicly listed since 1994. The company designs, sells, and builds single-family and multi-family homes across approximately thirteen U.S. states under brand differentiators such as Choice Plans (customizable floorplans), Mortgage Choice (competitive lender program), Style Choice (interior personalization), and Livable Features (accessibility options). Beazer markets itself as "America's #1 Energy-Efficient Homebuilder," citing homes that are 44% more efficient than the average HERS-rated new home and shipping whole-house ERV ventilation in 100% of homes. As of the most recent public data point (FY2016 10-K), Beazer reported revenue of $1.822B, delivered 5,419 homes, operated 161 active communities, and employed approximately 1,100 people. The company has no public developer program or external APIs; its digital surface is a consumer-facing marketing/community-finder website plus an investor relations portal.

name: Becton Dickinson
description: Becton Dickinson (BD) is a global medical technology company that develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices, instrument systems, and reagents. In October 2025, BD launched the BD Incada Connected Care Platform, an AI-enabled, cloud-based platform built on AWS that unifies data from nearly 3 million connected BD devices including infusion pumps, patient monitors, and pharmacy robotics. BD also produces the Pyxis medication management system and integrates with EMRs via HL7 FHIR standards for clinical data exchange.

name: Belden

The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

name: Benchmark Electronics
description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

description: Bright Horizons Family Solutions Inc. The company operates more than 1,000 early-education and child-care centers across the US, UK, Netherlands, and India, serving roughly 1,450 employer clients through three core lines: Full Service Center-Based Child Care (on-site and near-site centers for employer-sponsored families), Back-Up Care (last-minute child, adult/elder, and pet care via in-home and in-center networks), and Educational Advisory Services. description: 'Profile for Camping World Holdings in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 555).'

name: Capital One
description: Capital One is a financial services company offering credit cards, checking and savings accounts, loans, and auto financing in the United States. Through the Capital One DevExchange developer program, the bank publishes a catalog of production APIs for account lookup, transaction authorizations, credit offers, customer transactions, credit card applications, auto financing, proactive prescreen, partner account summary, shop with rewards, and public key sharing for client authentication. OAuth 2.0 secures access and a public sandbox supports pre-production integration.

name: Capri Holdings
description: Capri Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Capri Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Cardinal Health
description: Cardinal Health is a Fortune 15 global integrated healthcare services and products company that provides pharmaceutical distribution, medical-surgical product distribution, and customized solutions for hospitals, health systems, pharmacies, ambulatory surgery centers, clinical laboratories, and physician offices. Cardinal Health does not publish a public developer portal, but it exchanges high volumes of B2B trading data with customers and suppliers via standard X12 EDI transactions (850, 810, 855, 856, 846, 832, 867) over AS2, SFTP, and private API channels. Third-party EDI platforms such as Orderful, Crossfire, SPS Commerce, Zenbridge, DataTrans, Alluvia, ConnectPointz, and Spark Shipping offer managed connectors into Cardinal Health for order-to-cash, inventory, and supply-chain automation.

name: Carlisle Companies
description: Carlisle Companies Incorporated (NYSE: CSL) is a global diversified manufacturer of highly engineered building envelope products and solutions, serving commercial and residential construction, insulation, roofing, waterproofing, and specialty markets. Carlisle's primary operating segment is Carlisle Construction Materials (CCM), which includes brands such as Carlisle SynTec Systems, Hunter Panels, Henry Company, MB Technology, and WIP Industrial. Carlisle does not publish a public developer API; distributors and direct contractors transact through the Carlisle Customer Success Portal, and commercial trading partners integrate with Carlisle using standard X12 EDI transactions (850, 855, 856, 810) over AS2/SFTP.

name: CarMax
description: CarMax (NYSE: KMX) is the largest retailer of used cars in the United States, operating an omnichannel business that spans brick-and-mortar stores, carmax.com online purchasing, home delivery, financing, appraisals, and trade-ins. CarMax does not publish a public developer portal, but its engineering organization operates an extensive internal API program built around distinct API roles (Data Access Layer, Business Logic Layer, Server-Driven UI, Backend for Frontend). Public-facing APIs documented by the CarMax Engineering Blog include a Store Locations API and a Vehicle Inventory API, and CarMax has publicly discussed a Server-Driven UI API that controls vehicle search filters across web and mobile. Partner and syndication integrations are handled case by case rather than through a self-service portal.

name: Carpenter Technology
description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

name: Carrier Global
description: Carrier Global Corporation is a global provider of healthy, safe, sustainable, and intelligent building and cold-chain solutions, spanning HVAC, refrigeration, fire, security, and building automation technologies. Its digital ecosystem includes the Lynx Fleet telematics platform (Lynx APIs for transport refrigeration units), the Abound building management platform, i-Vu and Carrier Comfort Network for commercial building automation, and the Carrier SmartHome app for residential smart thermostats.

name: Carter's
description: Carter's is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Carter's API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Carter's
description: Carter's, Inc. is the largest branded marketer of young children's apparel in the United States, operating the Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, and Skip Hop brands. Its customer-facing digital surface includes carters.com and carters.com/cart e-commerce, mobile apps, a rewards program, and vendor / supply-chain integrations, but no public developer API or partner program is currently published.

name: Carvana
description: Carvana is an e-commerce platform for buying, selling, and financing used cars online, featuring home delivery or pickup at its distinctive car vending machines. Its primary developer-facing integration surface is the Carvana Partner REST API (published on Azure API Management at api-developer.carvana.com) which enables authorized rental companies, wholesalers, and fleet partners to post, update, and manage inventory in Carvana's catalog. A Carvana Collective API (api.collective.carvana.com) supports partner-collective workflows, and Carvana also distributes inventory data via AWS Data Exchange.

name: Casey's General Stores
description: Casey's General Stores is one of the largest convenience store chains in the United States, operating more than 2,900 stores selling fuel, made-from-scratch pizza, prepared food, and other convenience items primarily in small midwestern communities. Casey's is a publicly traded Fortune 500 company (NASDAQ: CASY) and offers a mobile app for pizza ordering, delivery, and its Casey's Rewards loyalty program. No public developer APIs have been documented; partner and supplier integrations are managed privately.

name: Catalent
description: Catalent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Catalent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Caterpillar
description: Caterpillar Inc. (NYSE: CAT) is the world's leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives. Its digital arm, Cat Digital, publishes developer APIs through the Cat Digital Marketplace (digital.cat.com) covering fleet, asset, fuel, and worksite telematics built on top of the Cat Connect and VisionLink data platforms.

name: Cavco Industries
description: Cavco Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cavco Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: CBOE
description: 'Fortune 1000 company CBOE. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.'

name: CBRE
description: CBRE Group, Inc. (NYSE: CBRE) is the world's largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with 155,000 professionals across 500+ offices in 100+ countries. CBRE provides advisory and transaction, project management, property management, valuation, investment management, and consulting services. Its technology arm publishes developer APIs through developer.cbre.com that expose property, analytics, and facilities data to partners.

name: CBS (Paramount Global)
description: CBS is the flagship broadcast television network of Paramount Global (NASDAQ: PARA, PARAA). It encompasses CBS Entertainment, CBS News, CBS Sports, CBS Stations (owned and operated), and feeds Paramount+ streaming service. CBS does not publish a consumer developer portal. Partner, syndication, advertising, and distribution APIs are operated privately through Paramount Global's business development, ad sales, and affiliate operations teams.

name: CDK Global
description: CDK Global is the dominant U.S. dealer management system (DMS) provider, serving roughly 15,000 automotive dealerships with software covering sales, F&I, fixed operations, parts, CRM, and digital retail. CDK was spun out of ADP in 2014 and acquired by Brookfield Business Partners in July 2022 for $8.3B (taken private). The company operates the Fortellis platform — a developer marketplace and integration hub with 135+ published APIs, 425+ marketplace apps, 82,000+ dealer integrations, and 6.7B+ API transactions per year — exposing CDK DMS data to ISVs, OEMs, and third-party automotive systems. CDK suffered a major BlackSuit ransomware attack on June 19, 2024, paying ~$25M in bitcoin to restore service over roughly two weeks; the outage caused an estimated $605M in dealer losses and triggered numerous lawsuits.

name: CDW
description: CDW is a leading multi-brand provider of information technology solutions to business, government, education, and healthcare customers. CDW offers eProcurement integration capabilities including a Catalog API, PunchOut (cXML/OCI), electronic purchase ordering, and electronic invoicing to enable procurement system integration with partners such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, and Jaggaer.

name: Celanese
description: Celanese Corporation is a global chemical and specialty materials company that produces high-performance engineered polymers and acetyl products used across automotive, medical, consumer, and industrial applications. Celanese has no publicly documented developer API; digital engagement is delivered through the Chemille digital materials assistant for product search and selection, and a Cognite Data Fusion based manufacturing data platform for internal operations.

name: Celgene
description: Celgene Corporation was a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of innovative therapies for cancer and immune-inflammatory diseases. Celgene was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) in November 2019 and its operations are now consolidated under BMS. No public developer API has been identified; engagement is organized through BMS clinical trials, study connect, and investigator-sponsored research portals.

name: Centene
description: Centene Corporation is a leading managed care organization providing government-sponsored healthcare programs including Medicaid, Medicare, and Health Insurance Marketplace plans. Centene operates a developer portal at partners.centene.com publishing FHIR-based interoperability APIs under the 21st Century Cures Act and CMS Interoperability and Patient Access Rule, including Patient Access, Provider Directory, and Provider RTR (Payer Data Exchange) APIs.

name: CenterPoint Energy
description: CenterPoint Energy is a domestic energy delivery company that provides electric transmission and distribution, natural gas distribution, and energy services operations serving residential, commercial, and industrial customers across multiple U.S. states. Developer-facing interfaces include the Smart Meter Texas (SMT) Usage History Inquiry API, Green Button Connect My Data exports for authorized third-party access to customer interval usage, and the Centerpoint Connect service API at api-portal.centerpointconnect.io used by contractor and field-service integrations.

name: Central Garden and Pet
description: Central Garden and Pet is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Central Garden and Pet API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Centric Brands
description: Centric Brands LLC is a New York-headquartered global lifestyle brand management and product-development platform formed in October 2018 when Differential Brands Group (NASDAQ: DFBG) acquired Global Brands Group's $1.2B North American licensing business. The company designs, sources, markets, and distributes apparel, accessories, footwear, beauty, and entertainment-licensed products across men's, women's, kids', accessories, and entertainment segments. Its mission is "to be a leading global apparel & accessories company with a portfolio of iconic licensed and owned brands that delight retailers and consumers of all ages." Centric filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 18, 2020 and emerged in October 2020 under control of secured creditors led by Blackstone's GSO Capital Partners, Ares Management, and HPS Investment Partners. The company is led by CEO Jason Rabin (since 2018) and operates ~20 global offices across New York (HQ), Los Angeles, Greensboro, Montreal, London, Amsterdam, Hong Kong, and multiple cities in China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Vietnam. Owned brands include Hudson Jeans, Buffalo Jeans, Robert Graham, Joe's Jeans, Hervé Léger, Favorite Daughter, and AllSaints; licensed apparel brands include Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, Nautica, Spyder, IZOD, Van Heusen, Kate Spade New York, Coach, Michael Kors, Frye, Timberland, Lucky Brand, Juicy Couture, Under Armour, and Off-White; the entertainment licensing portfolio spans 70+ properties including Disney, Marvel, Warner Bros., DC, Nintendo, Hasbro, Mattel, Nickelodeon, Netflix, Pokémon, Sanrio, Paw Patrol, and the NFL/MLB/NBA/NHL via Sports & Entertainment Licensing. Centric Brands operates "11 end-to-end Ecommerce sites," a 3D design and art studio in Greensboro, and a New York City photo/video studio. The company has no public developer program, no documented public APIs, and no public source code repositories; its two namesake GitHub organizations (centric-brands, Centricbrands) are private placeholders with zero public repos.

name: Century Communities
description: Century Communities is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Century Communities API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: CenturyLink (Lumen Technologies)
description: CenturyLink is the residential broadband and home services brand of Lumen Technologies, a Fortune 500 telecommunications provider operating one of the largest fiber networks in North America. Following the Level 3 acquisition and rebrand to Lumen, CenturyLink's developer surface is exposed through the Lumen Developer Center and Lumen API Marketplace, which publish REST APIs secured by OAuth 2.0 for enterprise location qualification, quote-to-order, provisioning, billing, notifications, CDN and edge compute, DDoS mitigation, and Public Sector networking products.

name: Cerner (Oracle Health)
description: Cerner is a global healthcare technology company that designs and develops electronic health record (EHR) and health information technology solutions for hospitals, clinics, and integrated delivery networks. Cerner was acquired by Oracle in June 2022 and is now branded as Oracle Health, with the Cerner Millennium EHR platform's developer program operating as the Oracle Health Developer Program. Millennium exposes HL7 FHIR R4 and DSTU2 APIs, SMART on FHIR app launching, Bulk FHIR, the CareAware device and integration APIs, and the Code Console developer portal for registering applications and obtaining sandbox and production credentials.

name: CF Industries Holdings
description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

name: Change Healthcare
description: Change Healthcare is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Change Healthcare API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Charles River Laboratories International
description: 'Profile for Charles River Laboratories International in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 855).'

name: Charles Schwab
description: Charles Schwab is a financial services company providing brokerage, banking, asset management, and financial advisory services to individual investors and independent investment advisors. The Schwab Developer Portal exposes Trader APIs that let registered applications access account balances, positions, and orders, place equity and option trades, and consume real-time and historical market data through OAuth 2.0-secured REST endpoints.

name: Charter Communications
description: Charter Communications, Inc. is a leading broadband connectivity company and cable operator serving more than 32 million customers in 41 states through its Spectrum brand. Charter offers internet, TV, mobile, and voice services to residential and business customers, and exposes developer APIs through the Spectrum Enterprise portal for service ticketing and carrier serviceability, and through the Bryte IQ Network-as-a-Service platform built on the Linux Foundation CAMARA project.

name: Cheesecake Factory
description: 'Profile for Cheesecake Factory in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 876).'

name: Chemours
description: 'Fortune 1000 company Chemours. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.'

name: Chemtura
description: Chemtura Corporation was a global specialty chemicals company that developed, manufactured, and marketed chemical intermediates, additives, specialty chemicals, urethanes, organometallics, and modern plastics. In April 2017, Chemtura was acquired by LANXESS AG, the German specialty chemicals company headquartered in Cologne, and its operations were integrated into LANXESS's Performance Materials and other business segments. Chemtura products are now marketed and supported through LANXESS, which continues to serve agriculture, animal care, mobility, consumer goods, electrical and electronics, energy, food, and healthcare end markets.

name: Chesapeake Energy
description: Chesapeake Energy Corporation was an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, focused on unconventional natural gas and oil fields onshore in the United States. In October 2024, Chesapeake combined with Southwestern Energy to form Expand Energy Corporation, which now operates as the largest natural gas producer in the United States. Chesapeake Energy does not currently expose a public developer API; royalty owners and partners interact through the Owner Online Accounts portal, and investors are served via the Expand Energy investor relations site.

name: Chevron
description: Chevron Corporation is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, with operations across upstream exploration and production, downstream refining and marketing, and the production and transportation of crude oil, natural gas, refined fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals, and renewable fuels. Chevron is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and operates globally under brands including Chevron, Texaco, and Caltex. Chevron does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; supplier and partner integrations are handled through the Chevron Invoice and Payment Status (CIPS) system and the Supplier Relations channels, and investors and stakeholders are served through corporate, sustainability, and IR websites.

name: Chewy
description: Chewy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American online retailer of pet food, pet products, prescription medications, and veterinary services headquartered in Plantation, Florida. Chewy is one of the largest e-commerce pet retailers in the United States and supports a customer-focused operating model centered on subscription Autoship orders, Chewy Pharmacy prescription fulfillment, Connect with a Vet telehealth, and Chewy Health insurance. Chewy provides vendor and supplier integration primarily through the Dsco supplier integration platform rather than a public consumer-facing developer API. The Dsco-based integration supports core EDI transactions for purchase orders, inventory updates, shipment confirmations, and invoices, enabling brands and third-party logistics providers to connect with Chewy's e-commerce marketplace.

name: Chico's FAS
description: Chico's FAS, Inc. is an American women's specialty retailer headquartered in Fort Myers, Florida, operating and franchising stores and websites under the Chico's, White House Black Market, and Soma brands. The company is a leading omni-channel specialty retailer of private branded sophisticated, casual-to-dressy clothing, intimates, sleepwear, and related accessories, with more than 1,400 retail and outlet stores in the United States and a substantial e-commerce footprint. Chico's FAS is part of the KnitWell Group portfolio. Chico's FAS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are coordinated through corporate channels and the loyalty/credit card partnership with Synchrony and Mastercard.

name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
description: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a Fortune 500 fast-casual restaurant chain serving burritos, bowls, tacos, salads, and quesadillas made with responsibly sourced, classically-cooked, real ingredients. Founded in 1993 in Denver, Colorado and headquartered in Newport Beach, California, Chipotle operates more than 3,500 restaurants across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. The company is widely recognized as a digital ordering and loyalty leader in the restaurant industry through its Chipotle Rewards program, native iOS and Android apps, and digital ordering platforms (web ordering, group ordering, and catering). Chipotle does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API catalog; partner integrations such as third-party delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) are managed through bilateral agreements, and supplier and franchise integrations occur through internal portals.

name: CHS Inc.
description: CHS Inc. is a Fortune 500 diversified, integrated, global agricultural cooperative owned by farmers, ranchers, cooperatives, and individual producers. Headquartered in Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota, CHS describes itself as the largest farmer-owned cooperative in the United States, with more than 750 member cooperatives, 75,000+ individual producer-owners, and 20,000+ preferred stockholders. The cooperative serves customers in 65 countries through three primary business divisions: Agriculture (crop nutrients, crop protection, precision agriculture, seed, animal nutrition, and oilseed products), Energy (refined fuels, propane, lubricants, pipelines, terminals, and renewable fuels under the Cenex brand), and Services (hedging, payment solutions, transportation, and capital services). Major brands include Cenex, Allegiant (seed), Payback (animal nutrition), and N-Edge (crop nutrients). CHS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are provided through digital platforms such as MyCHS (online portal for grain tickets, billing, and payments) and CHS Connect (digital self-service for crop protection and energy wholesale customers).

name: Chubb
description: Chubb Limited is the world's largest publicly traded property and casualty (P&C) insurance company, serving consumers, small businesses, and multinational corporations across 54 countries and territories. Chubb offers commercial and personal property and casualty insurance, personal accident and supplemental health insurance, reinsurance, and life insurance. The company manages more than $200B in global assets, paid $21B in claims (2023), and offers more than 200 insurance products and services. Key personal lines include homeowners, auto, valuables (jewelry, arts, wine), boat and yacht, pet (through a Healthy Paws partnership), and travel insurance. Commercial lines include small business, accident and health, commercial package, cyber, management liability, marine, professional liability, workers' compensation, and industry-specialty programs (construction, financial institutions, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, real estate, technology, climate). Chubb Studio is the company's embedded insurance technology platform offering APIs and SDKs for partners to integrate Chubb insurance products into their own digital experiences.

name: Church and Dwight
description: Church & Dwight Co., Inc. is a Fortune 500 American consumer packaged goods (CPG) company headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, that manufactures and markets a portfolio of household, personal care, health and wellness, beauty, and specialty products. Best known as the parent company of the Arm & Hammer baking soda brand (the company's flagship since 1846), Church & Dwight operates through three reporting segments: Consumer Domestic, Consumer International, and Specialty Products Division. The company's brand portfolio includes Arm & Hammer, Trojan, OxiClean, Vitafusion, L'il Critters, Therabreath, Hero (Mighty Patch), Batiste, Waterpik, OraJel, Nair, Spinbrush, First Response, RepHresh, Zicam, Flawless, Toppik, Viviscal, Kaboom, Orange Glo, XTRA laundry detergent, and Arrid antiperspirant. Church & Dwight does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are managed through internal portals, and consumer experiences focus on brand websites, e-commerce direct-to-consumer storefronts, and the Innovation Portal for external R&D partnerships.

name: Ciena
description: Ciena Corporation is a global networking equipment, software, and services vendor focused on optical and packet networking, SDN, and service automation. This index covers Ciena's open APIs across the Blue Planet automation platform, the Ciena MCP (Manage, Control, and Plan) NMS, and the Emulation Cloud developer environment, exposing TM Forum Open APIs, MEF Lifecycle Service Orchestration (LSO) APIs (Legato, Sonata), and ONAP-aligned policy controls for telecom carriers and managed service providers.

name: Cigna
description: Cigna Healthcare is a leading global health services company offering medical, dental, behavioral, and pharmacy plans for individuals, families, and employers. The Cigna Developer Portal exposes CMS-mandated FHIR APIs for Patient Access, Provider Directory, Drug Formulary, and Provider Access, along with member and provider service APIs that enable third-party applications, electronic health record systems, and partners to access member health data with consent and look up Cigna network providers and formulary information.

name: Cimarex Energy
description: Cimarex Energy was an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations focused in the Permian Basin and the Mid-Continent. In October 2021 Cimarex Energy combined with Cabot Oil & Gas Corporation to form Coterra Energy (NYSE: CTRA). No public Cimarex-branded developer APIs exist; all current digital channels and any future API offerings are part of Coterra Energy.

name: Cincinnati Financial
description: Cincinnati Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: CINF) is a property and casualty insurer headquartered in Fairfield, Ohio, that markets a full suite of business, home, auto, and life insurance products plus investment services exclusively through a network of independent insurance agencies. Cincinnati Financial does not currently operate a public developer portal or expose customer-facing APIs; agency, claims, and policyholder access is delivered through web portals (cinfin.com, onlineservice.cinfin.com, and the Cincinnati Insurance Mobile App), with technical integrations for appointed agencies handled directly by Cincinnati Insurance IT support.

name: Cinemark Holdings
description: Cinemark Holdings is one of the largest motion picture exhibitors in the world, operating theatres across the United States and Latin America under the Cinemark, Century, Tinseltown, Rave, and CineArts brands. Cinemark does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer portal; ticketing, showtime, and loyalty integrations are typically delivered through partner agreements and third-party aggregators (Movio, Atom Tickets, Fandango).

name: Cintas
description: Cintas Corporation is a Fortune 500 provider of uniform rental, facility services, first aid and safety products, and fire protection services. Cintas does not currently publish a public developer portal; B2B integrations (ordering, EDI, route management, billing) are delivered to enterprise customers through the myCintas portal, the Cintas Partner Connect program, and account-managed EDI relationships.

name: CIRCOR International
description: CIRCOR International is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CIRCOR International API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Cisco
description: Cisco provides a comprehensive suite of APIs across its networking, security, collaboration, and cloud infrastructure

name: Cisco Systems
description: Cisco Systems is a global technology company providing networking, security, collaboration, and cloud infrastructure products. Cisco exposes its programmable surface through Cisco DevNet, a single developer portal that aggregates documentation, sandboxes, code exchange, and learning labs across the company's hardware and software portfolio. Major API domains include Catalyst Center and Meraki for network management, IOS XE RESTCONF for device-level programmability, Webex for collaboration, Secure Firewall and ISE for security, ThousandEyes and AppDynamics for observability, and Intersight for cloud-managed infrastructure. Authentication models vary by product line and include OAuth 2.0, API keys, basic-auth token exchange, and HTTP signature authentication.

name: CIT Group
description: CIT Group was a US financial holding company providing commercial financing, equipment leasing, factoring, and middle-market banking services. CIT was acquired by First Citizens BancShares in January 2022 and has been integrated into First Citizens Bank as the Commercial Banking division. CIT Group does not maintain a public developer portal and never published general-purpose REST APIs; legacy customer integrations were delivered through file-based ACH/wire feeds, the OneWest online banking platform, and partner-mediated treasury connectivity. New API-based integrations for the combined institution are now exposed through First Citizens Bank.

name: Citigroup
description: Citigroup is a global diversified financial services holding company providing consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services. Citi exposes its API surface through the Citi Developer Hub, a unified developer portal spanning the bank's retail, commercial, and Treasury and Trade Solutions (TTS) lines of business. Major API domains include CitiConnect for corporate treasury, Accounts and Transactions for retail, Money Movement for payment initiation, Customer Onboarding, Authorization, and utilities for FX rates and reference data. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 with mutual TLS for production endpoints.

name: Citrix
description: Citrix is a global software company providing virtualization, networking, workspace, and digital experience products that allow organizations to deliver applications and desktops securely from data centers and clouds to any device. Citrix exposes its programmable surface through the Citrix Cloud platform and developer.citrix.com / developer-docs.citrix.com, with REST APIs spanning Virtual Apps and Desktops, DaaS, Workspace, Citrix Cloud, ADC (NetScaler) NITRO, Endpoint Management, Secure Private Access, and Analytics. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens issued through Citrix Cloud customer-id-scoped credentials.

name: Clean Energy Fuels
description: Clean Energy Fuels is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Clean Energy Fuels API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Clean Harbors
description: Clean Harbors is the largest provider of environmental and industrial services in North America, delivering hazardous and non-hazardous waste management, emergency response, industrial cleaning, environmental remediation, and used-oil and solvent recycling through its Safety-Kleen subsidiary. Clean Harbors does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface; programmatic interfaces are limited to the authenticated customer portal at clhsaas.cleanharbors.com (CLH SaaS) for service requests, manifests, and reporting, and partner-mediated EDI feeds. Customers also use the EPA e-Manifest system for federally regulated hazardous-waste manifest tracking.

name: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings
description: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings is one of the largest out-of-home advertising companies in the world and a Fortune 1000 firm, operating billboards, street furniture, transit, airport, and digital out-of-home displays across the United States and select international markets. CCO operates the CCO.IO developer platform with the Automated Direct API at direct.cco.io for programmatic-direct buying of inventory, supports programmatic digital-out-of-home (pDOOH) buying through 21+ DSP partners using OpenRTB 2.6 with the DOOH extension, and offers RADAR, an audience and attribution data suite based on aggregated mobile location data. Open-source SDKs for the Automated Direct API are published under the ClearChannelOutdoor GitHub organization.

name: Clearwater Paper
description: Clearwater Paper is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Clearwater Paper API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: CME Group
description: CME Group is the world's largest derivatives exchange and operator of the CME, CBOT, NYMEX, and COMEX markets, offering futures and options across interest rates, equity indexes, foreign exchange, energy, agricultural products, and metals. CME Group exposes a portfolio of REST and streaming APIs through its Data Services Portal - including CME Reference Data API, Real-Time Futures and Options Data API, CME Term SOFR API, FedWatch API, Greeks and Implied Volatility API, EUR/USD Cross Currency Basis Index API, the CME ClearPort API for OTC trade submission, and iLink/MDP 3.0 connectivity to CME Globex for execution and market data.

name: CMS Energy
description: CMS Energy is an energy holding company whose primary subsidiary is Consumers Energy, an electric and natural gas utility serving customers in Michigan. Consumers Energy participates in the Green Button Connect My Data (GBCMD) program, exposing customer-authorized energy usage data to third parties via OAuth 2.0 - typically brokered through UtilityAPI - for use in energy management, demand response, EV charging, solar, and sustainability applications.

name: Cogent Communications
description: Cogent Communications is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cogent Communications API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Cognizant Technology Solutions
description: Cognizant Technology Solutions is a multinational information technology services and consulting company that provides digital, technology, consulting, and operations services to clients worldwide. Cognizant does not publish a general-purpose public REST API. Its developer-facing footprint is centered on the Cognizant Neuro AI platform family (Neuro AI Decisioning, Neuro AI Enterprise Core, Neuro AI Engineering, Neuro AI for IT Operations) and the open-source Neuro SAN multi-agent orchestration framework released by Cognizant AI Lab. Other delivered platforms (BigFrame for mainframe data migration, ADM accelerators, industry vertical solutions) are typically engaged via consulting engagements rather than self-service APIs.

name: Coherent
description: Coherent Corp. is a Fortune 500 global leader in materials, networking, and laser technologies. The company designs and manufactures engineered materials, optoelectronic components, optical transceivers, laser systems, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment for AI infrastructure, datacommunications, industrial, aerospace and defense, life sciences, and consumer electronics markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Coherent. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

name: Colgate-Palmolive
description: Colgate-Palmolive Company is a global consumer-products manufacturer operating in oral care, personal care, home care, and pet nutrition through brands such as Colgate, Palmolive, Hill's Pet Nutrition, Speed Stick, Ajax, and Softsoap. Colgate-Palmolive does not publish a general-purpose public developer REST API. Its B2B integration footprint is centered on EDI exchanges with retail trading partners (X12 messages, AS2, VAN), supplier integrations through SAP Ariba, and internal corporate systems. There is also a corporate sustainability and ESG reporting surface, but it is not exposed as a developer API.

name: Colony Capital (DigitalBridge Group)
description: Colony Capital was a diversified real estate and hospitality investment firm founded by Tom Barrack in 1991. In June 2021 the company rebranded as DigitalBridge Group, Inc. (NYSE: DBRG) — completing a multi-year pivot from traditional real estate to pure-play digital infrastructure investing. The Boca Raton, FL-based alternative asset manager now operates exclusively across five digital infrastructure categories: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber networks, small cells, and edge infrastructure. DigitalBridge manages approximately $119B in assets across 45+ portfolio companies including Vantage Data Centers, DataBank, Switch, Vertical Bridge, Zayo Group, GD Towers, Boingo Wireless, AtlasEdge, Scala Data Centers, Yondr Group, and ExteNet Systems. In December 2025 SoftBank Group announced a definitive agreement to acquire DigitalBridge for approximately $4 billion, with the deal expected to close in the second half of 2026. DigitalBridge itself publishes no developer API, SDK, or public OpenAPI surface — it is a holding company whose programmable surface lives inside its individual portfolio companies (e.g., Zayo, DataBank, Switch), each of which is profiled separately in the API Evangelist network.

name: Columbia Sportswear
description: Columbia Sportswear is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of outdoor, active, and everyday lifestyle apparel, footwear, accessories, and equipment under the Columbia, Mountain Hardwear, SOREL, and prAna brands. Columbia Sportswear Digital operates a partner-focused developer portal on Microsoft Azure API Management at columbia.portal.azure-api.net, exposing APIs for Order Management, Consumer Management, Product Lifecycle Management, Cognitive, Weather, and Translation. The developer portal is gated: registered partners create an account, browse products and APIs, request subscription keys, and integrate against the published endpoints. The company also exchanges traditional EDI documents (POs, ASNs, invoices) with retail trading partners through providers like TrueCommerce and eZCom.

name: Comcast
description: Comcast Corporation is a global media and technology company with two primary businesses, Comcast Cable (Xfinity) and NBCUniversal, providing video, internet, voice, wireless, and entertainment services to residential and business customers. Comcast publishes a public developer program centered on the Firebolt application platform for connected TV experiences, along with authentication and content ingest endpoints used by NBCUniversal media partners. The Firebolt SDK family is used by app developers to write apps once and deploy across Xfinity X1, Xfinity Flex, Sky Q, and other Comcast set-top boxes and connected devices.

name: Comerica
description: Comerica Incorporated is a Texas-headquartered financial services holding company providing retail, commercial, and wealth-management banking across the United States. As of April 2026, Comerica does not publish a public developer API portal. Customer banking data flows for fintech integrations are reached indirectly through US open-banking aggregators (Plaid, Tink, TrueLayer, MX) and through emerging Financial Data Exchange (FDX) APIs required under CFPB Section 1033 once the rule is no longer subject to judicial stay. Internal commercial APIs (treasury management, cash positioning, ACH initiation) are available to customers under direct contract through Comerica Treasury Management, but are not publicly documented.

name: Comfort Systems USA
description: Comfort Systems USA is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Comfort Systems USA API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Commercial Metals Company
description: Commercial Metals Company (CMC) is a Fortune 500 manufacturer, recycler, and marketer of steel and metal products serving the construction, energy, and manufacturing industries. CMC was the first US steel company to launch an online customer portal (myCMC), but does not currently publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI specifications. Programmatic integrations with myCMC (order management, shipping, invoicing) are typically established through direct contracts with CMC's IT organization rather than via a self-service developer program.

name: CommScope Holding
description: CommScope is a global provider of communications-network infrastructure, including fiber-optic and copper cabling, antenna systems, and cloud- managed enterprise networking. Following its acquisitions of ARRIS (2019) and the Ruckus Wi-Fi business, CommScope's primary public developer surface is the RUCKUS One API, a JSON REST surface for managing Wi-Fi networks, ICX switches, access points, venues, and managed-service-provider delegation. Companion product lines (RUCKUS Cloud, RUCKUS IoT, ICX RESTCONF, SmartZone, Cloudpath, Unleashed Multi- Site Manager, SmartCell Insight) ship their own REST/RESTCONF APIs and are documented through the CommScope and RUCKUS Networks developer centers.

name: Community Health Systems
description: Community Health Systems (CHS) is a Fortune 500 hospital operator that owns, leases, and operates general acute care hospitals across the United States. In compliance with the CMS Interoperability and Patient Access Final Rule (CMS-9115-F), CHS publishes FHIR R4 healthcare interoperability APIs that allow third-party applications to access patient demographics and clinical data, adjudicated claims and encounters, formulary information, and provider directory data. The APIs use the HL7 FHIR R4 standard and SMART-on-FHIR authorization for patient-scoped access.

name: Compass
description: Compass is a leading real estate technology company headquartered in New York City that provides a tech-enabled brokerage platform connecting agents, buyers, and sellers across the United States. The company combines residential real estate services with proprietary software for agents, including marketing, client management, and listing tools. Compass does not currently publish a public developer API portal.

name: Computer Sciences Corporation
description: Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) was a multinational information technology services and professional services company. On April 1, 2017, CSC merged with the Enterprise Services line of business of Hewlett Packard Enterprise to form DXC Technology, retiring the standalone CSC brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; CSC did not publish any public developer APIs and the entity is no longer actively operated under this name.

name: Conagra Brands
description: Conagra Brands is a leading North American branded consumer packaged goods (CPG) food company headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. Its portfolio of iconic frozen, refrigerated, and shelf-stable brands includes Marie Callender's, Healthy Choice, Slim Jim, Reddi-wip, Hunt's, Banquet, Birds Eye, Duncan Hines, and Orville Redenbacher's. Conagra internally describes itself as API-first across its digital estate, but does not publish any public developer APIs at this time. Partner integrations such as foodservice, retail, and supplier portals are managed via direct B2B agreements rather than a public developer surface.

name: ConAgra Foods
description: ConAgra Foods, Inc. was the prior corporate name of Conagra Brands. In 2015 the company spun off its foodservice ingredients business as Lamb Weston and renamed the remaining packaged-foods business to Conagra Brands, Inc. This profile is preserved as a historical alias; the active company profile lives at the conagra-brands repository. No public developer APIs were ever published under the ConAgra Foods brand.

name: Concentrix
description: Concentrix is a global technology and services leader providing customer experience (CX) management, digital transformation, and technology consulting across approximately 2,000 brands worldwide. Its product suite spans the iX product line (including iX Hello and iX Hero agentic AI assistants) and the Catalyst experience transformation and technology consultancy. Concentrix does not publish a public developer API; the iX product suite and Catalyst services are delivered via managed engagements and enterprise integrations rather than a self-service developer portal.

name: Concho Resources
description: Concho Resources, Inc. was an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the acquisition, development, exploration, and production of oil and natural gas properties primarily in the Permian Basin of West Texas and southeast New Mexico. On January 15, 2021, ConocoPhillips completed an all-stock acquisition of Concho Resources at a total enterprise value of $13.3 billion, retiring the Concho brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Concho no longer operates under this name and never published any public developer APIs.

name: Conduent
description: Conduent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Conduent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: ConocoPhillips
description: ConocoPhillips is a leading global exploration and production company, headquartered in Houston, Texas, that is uniquely equipped to deliver reliable, responsibly produced oil and natural gas. The company operates in more than a dozen countries with conventional and unconventional crude oil, natural gas, LNG, and natural gas liquids assets. ConocoPhillips does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations portal, a vendor relations portal (powered by third-party platforms such as GEP and Taulia), an LNG technology and licensing program, and a custom sustainability report builder.

name: CONSOL Energy
description: CONSOL Energy was a Pittsburgh-based coal mining company that produced high-quality bituminous coal from underground mines for sale to electric utilities, steelmakers, and industrial customers. In 2025 CONSOL Energy merged with Arch Resources to form Core Natural Resources, and the consolenergy.com domain now redirects to corenaturalresources.com. The combined company does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations site, a suppliers page (with downloadable terms, conditions, and a Supplier Code of Conduct), and corporate sustainability/safety disclosures.

name: Consolidated Edison
description: Consolidated Edison, Inc. (Con Edison) is a Fortune 500 holding company that, through its subsidiaries, provides electric, natural gas, and steam service to customers in New York City and Westchester County. Con Edison does not publish a general-purpose developer portal; programmatic data access is delivered through the Green Button Connect My Data (GBC) program, which lets authorized third parties retrieve customer energy usage data via the NAESB Energy Services Provider Interface (ESPI) standard once the customer grants consent through Con Edison's authorization portal.

name: Constellation Brands
description: Constellation Brands is a Fortune 500 producer and marketer of beer, wine, and spirits brands such as Corona, Modelo, Robert Mondavi, and Casa Noble. Constellation publishes a partner-oriented API catalog at dev.cbrands.com that exposes product, brand, and digital-asset data (bottle shots, tasting notes, hot sheets, shelf talkers, neck hangers, recipes, and an items product API) to distributors, retailers, and on-premise partners. Most endpoints require an API key issued through the developer registration process.

name: Constellation Energy
description: Constellation Energy Corporation is a Fortune 500 clean-energy producer and competitive retail electricity and natural gas supplier in the United States, generating power from a fleet of nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar facilities. Constellation does not publish a public developer portal; programmatic interactions are delivered to enterprise and large commercial customers through the Energy Manager platform (account-managed onboarding, no public API specifications) and consumer interactions are handled through the My Constellation account portal. EDI 867 (usage) and 810 (invoice) remain the most common machine-to-machine integration paths and are arranged on a contract-by-contract basis.

name: Cooper
description: 'Profile for Cooper in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 848).'

name: Cooper Tire & Rubber
description: Cooper Tire & Rubber Company is an American manufacturer of replacement tires for passenger cars, light trucks, SUVs, and commercial vehicles, founded in 1914 and headquartered in Findlay, Ohio. Cooper was acquired by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company in June 2021 and now operates as a subsidiary, retaining the Cooper brand alongside Goodyear. The Cooper brand portfolio covers all-season, winter, all-terrain, and sport performance tires distributed through retailers and dealers worldwide. Cooper Tire does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence is consumer-facing tire selection, retailer locators, and post-purchase tire registration.

name: Copart
description: 'Fortune 1000 company Copart. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.'

name: Core & Main
description: Core & Main is a leading specialty distributor of water, wastewater, storm drainage, and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, contractors, and engineers across the United States. As a Fortune 500 company, Core & Main operates more than 320 branch locations and provides products and services for water infrastructure, geosynthetics, fusible HDPE pipe, smart metering, fire protection, and erosion control.

name: Core-Mark Holding
description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.

name: Corebridge Financial
description: Corebridge Financial (formerly AIG Life and Retirement) is one of the largest and most established retirement and insurance solutions providers in the United States. Spun off from AIG in September 2022 in the largest IPO of that year, Corebridge provides retirement solutions, life insurance, fixed and variable annuities, and institutional products. The company is a leading retirement plan provider for K-12 schools, healthcare, government, higher education, and other not-for-profit institutions. Corebridge Financial does not currently publish a public developer API; participant and plan sponsor access is provided through dedicated portals.

name: Cornerstone Building Brands
description: Cornerstone Building Brands is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cornerstone Building Brands API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Corning
description: Corning Incorporated is a Fortune 500 American technology company that specializes in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics. Founded in 1851, Corning manufactures specialty glass, ceramics, and related materials and technologies for industrial and scientific applications. Corning's businesses include Optical Communications (fiber optic cable and hardware), Display Technologies (LCD and OLED glass substrates), Specialty Materials (Gorilla Glass for mobile devices), Environmental Technologies (ceramic substrates and filters for emissions control), and Life Sciences (laboratory glassware, cell culture, and bioprocess products). Corning does not publish a public developer API.

name: Corteva
description: Corteva Agriscience is a publicly traded, Fortune 500 global pure-play agriculture company that provides farmers around the world with one of the most complete portfolios in the industry, including a balanced and diverse mix of seed, crop protection, and digital products. Corteva was formed as the spinoff of the agriculture division of DowDuPont in June 2019. The company markets seeds under the Pioneer, Brevant, and other brands and crop protection products including herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, and biologicals. Corteva also operates Granular, a farm management software platform with insights and analytics products. A public developer API is not currently published; growers access tools through the Granular Insights and Granular Link platforms.

name: Costco Wholesale
description: Costco Wholesale Corporation is a Fortune 500 American multinational membership-only big-box retail chain that operates warehouse clubs offering a wide selection of merchandise at discounted prices. Costco does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading partner integrations are conducted through EDI and B2B channels using ANSI X12 transactions and the Costco Supplier Portal. Costco operates an e-commerce site, the Costco Travel and Costco Pharmacy properties, and the Costco Photo Center.

name: Coterra Energy
description: Coterra Energy is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Coterra Energy API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Coty
description: Coty Inc. is one of the world's largest beauty companies with an iconic portfolio of brands across fragrance, color cosmetics, skin and body care. The company operates two divisions: Prestige (premium fragrance, cosmetics, and skincare brands such as Gucci, Burberry, Calvin Klein, Hugo Boss, Marc Jacobs, Tiffany, Chloe, Davidoff, Lancaster, philosophy, and Kylie Cosmetics) and Consumer Beauty (mass-market color cosmetics, hair care, and body care brands such as CoverGirl, Rimmel, Max Factor, Sally Hansen, Bourjois, and Adidas). Coty does not publish a public developer API; supplier and partner integrations occur through the Coty Supplier Portal and B2B / EDI channels.

name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
description: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. is an American chain of restaurants and gift shops with a Southern country theme, offering home-style meals and retail merchandise. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Lebanon, Tennessee, Cracker Barrel operates roughly 656 restaurant and retail locations across 44 U.S. states. No public API or developer portal is published; the company offers a consumer website, iOS and Android mobile ordering apps, To-Go and catering ordering, gift cards, and the Cracker Barrel Rewards loyalty program for guests.

name: Crane
description: Crane Co. (NYSE: CR) and its sister company Crane NXT (NYSE: CXT) are industrial manufacturing companies that resulted from the 2023 split of the legacy Crane Holdings, Co. Crane Co. is a diversified manufacturer of highly engineered industrial products serving aerospace and electronics, process flow technologies, and engineered materials markets. Crane NXT is a global leader in trusted technology solutions for payment, security, and authentication including currency, banknote, and authentication products. No public APIs or developer portals are published; integrations with industrial customers are arranged through enterprise channels.

name: Crane Worldwide Logistics
description: Crane Worldwide Logistics is a global third-party logistics provider delivering air freight, ocean freight, customs brokerage, warehousing, trucking, and supply chain solutions across more than 30 countries. Crane exposes a developer API portal powered by Tyk that gives partners and customers programmatic access to shipment, booking, and tracking data across the company's supply chain operations.

name: CrewAI Cloud
description: CrewAI Cloud (CrewAI AMP) is the managed Agent Management Platform for deploying, monitoring, scaling, and governing CrewAI multi-agent workflows in production. AMP exposes a per-crew REST API for kickoff, status, inputs, and human-in-the-loop resume operations, plus webhook streaming for task, step, and crew events. The platform ships in two deployment modes — AMP Cloud (managed, multi-tenant at app.crewai.com) and AMP Factory (self-hosted on AWS, Azure, or GCP) — and layers RBAC, SSO, secrets manager federation (AWS/Azure/GCP), agent and tool repositories, a marketplace, A2A communication, automations and triggers, traces with PII redaction, and observability exports on top of the open-source CrewAI framework.

name: CrossAmerica Partners
description: CrossAmerica Partners is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CrossAmerica Partners API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: CrowdStrike
description: CrowdStrike is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CrowdStrike API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Crown Castle
description: Crown Castle is a leading United States provider of shared communications infrastructure including cell towers, small cells, and fiber. Crown Castle owns and operates more than 40,000 cell towers and approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber, supporting wireless carriers, enterprises, and government customers with managed connectivity, dark fiber, optical encryption, ultra-low-latency transport, and managed SD-WAN services. Crown Castle does not currently publish a public developer API program; technical integrations are handled through customer and channel partner agreements.

name: Crown Holdings
description: Crown Holdings, Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacture, and sale of rigid packaging products for consumer goods, including metal beverage cans and ends, food cans, aerosol cans, specialty closures and promotional tins, as well as transit and protective packaging products for industrial markets. The company operates in more than 40 countries and supports customers with design, decoration, reprographics, compound development, pilot facilities, and seaming training services. Crown Holdings does not publish a public developer API program; technical collaboration with customers happens through B2B and EDI channels.

name: CSX Corporation
description: CSX Corporation is a Class I freight railroad operating one of the largest rail networks in the eastern United States, serving 23 states with roughly 20,000 route miles of track. CSX moves bulk commodities, intermodal shipments, and merchandise for industrial customers and operates the ShipCSX customer portal for shipment management, EDI integration, and freight tracking.

name: Cubic Corporation
description: Cubic Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cubic Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Cullen/Frost Bankers
description: Cullen/Frost Bankers is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cullen/Frost Bankers API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Cummins
description: Cummins is a global power leader that designs, manufactures, distributes, and services diesel and natural gas engines, electric and hybrid powertrains, electrified power systems, components such as filtration, aftertreatment, turbochargers, fuel systems, controls systems, air handling systems, automated transmissions, and electric power generation systems. Cummins serves customers in approximately 190 countries and territories through a network of more than 600 company-owned and independent distributor locations and approximately 7,200 dealer locations.

name: Curtiss-Wright
description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

name: CVS Health
description: CVS Health is a Fortune 50 healthcare services and retail pharmacy company. Its core operating units include CVS Pharmacy (retail pharmacy and mail-order), CVS Caremark (pharmacy benefit management / PBM), Aetna (health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, dental and vision), MinuteClinic (walk-in clinics), Oak Street Health (primary care for Medicare patients), and Signify Health (in-home health evaluations). CVS Health does not currently operate a public developer portal or generally available REST API. Programmatic integrations with CVS Pharmacy, Caremark, and Aetna are typically established through business partnership agreements, EDI / NCPDP pharmacy networks, and HIPAA-aligned interoperability channels (e.g., FHIR endpoints exposed to qualifying healthcare partners under regulatory mandates such as the CMS Interoperability Rule). Developer-facing artifacts in this index are limited to public marketing, corporate, and digital health references.

name: D.R. Horton
description: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder by volume in the United States, building and selling single-family homes in dozens of states across multiple price points. The company is a Fortune 500 enterprise with affiliated financial services including DHI Mortgage, DHI Title, and DRH Insurance.

name: Dana
description: Dana Incorporated is a global supplier of fully integrated drivetrain and electrified propulsion systems for passenger vehicles, commercial trucks, and off-highway equipment. Dana operates a developer portal at developer.danaaftermarket.com offering eight APIs for aftermarket parts search, availability, pricing, ordering, and shipment tracking across its global distribution network.

name: Dana Incorporated
description: Dana Incorporated is a global supplier of fully integrated drivetrain and electrified propulsion systems for passenger, commercial, and off-highway vehicles. Dana announced an agreement in 2025 for its Off-Highway business to be acquired by Allison Transmission. Dana's main public API surface is the Dana Aftermarket developer platform; this repository is an alias of the primary "dana" profile.

name: Danaher
description: Danaher Corporation is a global life sciences and diagnostics conglomerate whose operating companies include Beckman Coulter, Leica Microsystems, Cepheid, SCIEX, IDT, Cytiva, Abcam, Aldevron, Beckman Coulter Diagnostics, Radiometer, and others. Danaher itself does not publish a corporate-level developer API; product and service APIs are provided by individual operating companies under the Danaher portfolio.

name: Darden Restaurants
description: Darden Restaurants is the largest full-service restaurant company in the world, owning and operating brands such as Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Yard House, The Capital Grille, Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Eddie V's, Seasons 52, Bahama Breeze, Ruth's Chris Steak House, and Chuy's. Darden does not publish a public developer API; consumer-facing ordering and loyalty are exposed only via internal mobile apps and partnerships such as Uber for delivery.

name: Darling Ingredients
description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.

name: DaVita
description: DaVita Inc. is a Fortune 500 kidney care company operating in-center hemodialysis, home hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis programs in the United States and abroad, alongside transplant support, integrated kidney care, hospital partnerships, and clinical research. DaVita does not publish a public developer API; integration with the company is handled through patient-facing portals, payer and provider partnerships, and electronic health record data exchange standards.

name: DCP Midstream (Acquired by Phillips 66)
description: DCP Midstream LLC was a Denver, Colorado-based natural gas gathering, processing, and NGL transportation company that operated as one of the largest U.S. producers and marketers of natural gas liquids. In June 2023, Phillips 66 completed the acquisition of all publicly traded common units of DCP Midstream LP for approximately $3.8 billion, taking its ownership stake to 86.8%. DCP Midstream and Phillips 66 Partners were subsequently merged into Phillips 66's NGL and midstream business; the standalone brand, public filings, developer surface, and corporate website have been retired. The dcpmidstream.com domain no longer resolves to a working site, and there is no public DCP-branded developer portal, API reference, status page, or changelog. This repository documents DCP Midstream as a defunct entity absorbed into the Phillips 66 midstream organization.

name: Dean Foods
description: Dean Foods was a leading U.S. food and beverage company and one of the largest processors and direct-to-store distributors of fresh fluid milk and other dairy products. After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019, most of Dean Foods' assets were acquired by Dairy Farmers of America (DFA) in 2020. Dean Foods no longer operates as an independent company and does not publish a public developer API; surviving brands are now managed under DFA. This profile is retained for historical reference.

name: Delek US
description: Delek US is an alias for Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK), a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. The canonical profile for this company is maintained under aid delek-us-holdings; this entry exists as a name alias and references the corporate site. Delek does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

(NYSE: DK) is a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. Logistics assets are operated through Delek Logistics Partners (NYSE: DKL). The company provides investor relations and ESG reporting on its public website but does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

name: Dell Technologies
description: Dell Technologies is a global Fortune 500 technology company that designs, develops, manufactures, and supports a wide range of computing products, including PCs, servers, storage, networking equipment, and software services. Dell publishes a developer platform exposing APIs and SDKs for managing PowerEdge servers, PowerStore storage, PowerScale, OpenManage, APEX, and related infrastructure products, enabling automation of IT operations and integration into enterprise tooling.

name: Deloitte
description: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a network of member firms coordinated by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL). The organization spans approximately 150 countries and territories, has more than 180 years of history (founded 1845), and serves roughly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. Deloitte organizes delivery across four primary service lines — Audit & Assurance, Consulting, Tax, and Legal — plus specialized cross-functional practices including Business Process Solutions and Global Employer Services. Consulting offerings cover Customer, Cyber, Engineering / AI & Data, Enterprise Technology & Performance, Finance Transformation, Human Capital, Strategy & Transactions, and Risk / Regulatory & Forensic. Deloitte Digital is the technology-and-experience practice with alliances spanning Salesforce, Adobe, SAP, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, Shopify, Sitecore, and Genesys, and accelerators such as FrontOffice Advantage, Revenue Advantage, Agentic Marketing Cloud, CreativEdge, Blueprint, Content Studios, and TrustID. The organization serves six industries divided into twenty sectors: Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Health Care; and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. Deloitte Insights is the organization's research-publishing surface, organized into eight research centers — Cross-Industry, Economics, Consumer, Energy & Industrials, Financial Services, Government & Public Services, Life Sciences & Health Care, and Tech, Media & Telecom — producing flagship series including Tech Trends, Global Human Capital Trends, Digital Media Trends, TMT Predictions, FSI Predictions, the Weekly Global Economic Outlook, and the annual Industry Outlooks. The Deloitte AI Institute drives applied-AI research and points of view. Deloitte does not publish a public developer API or open developer portal at the corporate level. The Deloitte US Consulting GitHub organization is small (5 visible repositories, mostly archived upstream forks; the original artifact is `beacon`, a first-party web-analytics packaging library in TypeScript). Reader-facing distribution flows through MyDeloitte (personalized content + newsletter subscriptions), Dbriefs (live webcasts with CPE credit), the Deloitte Insights Magazine, and the YouTube channel; no public RSS index page was discoverable on www.deloitte.com at the path published in legacy archives.

name: Delta Air Lines
description: Delta Air Lines is a major U.S. airline providing scheduled air transportation for passengers and cargo throughout the United States and across the world. Delta operates a developer API portal for partner integrations covering flight search, flight offers, customer journey, loyalty, and operations data, with an emphasis on NDC-based content distribution.

name: Deluxe Corporation
description: Deluxe Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Deluxe Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

name: Denbury Resources
description: Denbury Resources (now Denbury Inc.) was an independent oil and natural gas company focused on enhanced oil recovery (EOR) using carbon dioxide injection in mature oil fields. Denbury was acquired by ExxonMobil in November 2023 and operates as a subsidiary inside ExxonMobil's Low Carbon Solutions business. Denbury does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

name: Dentsply Sirona
description: Dentsply Sirona is the world's largest manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, providing comprehensive solutions for dentists, dental laboratories, and dental specialists worldwide. The company exposes developer integrations through DS Core, an open cloud platform, and through the Dentsply Sirona Imaging modality API for intraoral imaging hardware.
